machine: Windows 11, Intel i9-14900HX (24 cores / 32 logical), RTX 4070 Laptop (unused by these runs)
protocol: WalkerRagdoll-v0, task_phase=recovery, reset_mode=mixed, random actions in [-1,1], 3s per measurement, envs_per_worker=1, sparse_info=true
notes: SyncVectorEnv throughput is flat in num_envs: stepping happens in the trainer thread, so 32 envs cost 32x the wall clock of one env and return the same ~1.5k steps/s.
The parallel backend's speedup grows with num_envs and only becomes worth the ~1s/worker startup from about 8-16 envs. This is why --vec-backend defaults to sync.
envs_per_worker was swept 1..8 at n=32 (light stack): 242, 220, 220, 190, 180, 184 vector steps/s. Grouping does not help, so one worker per env is the default.
sparse_info (omit the per-step info dict) moved n=32 from 151 to 210 vector steps/s on the light stack.
A single env spends ~40% of its step time in MuJoCo physics at RK4 dt=0.002 with frame_skip=5; the remaining Python in the reward path was reduced ~4x by the throughput rewrite.
